events.title: MacBook Air released
events.summary: Steve Jobs introduced the MacBook Air on January 29, 2008 — an ultraportable Mac slim enough to fit in a manila envelope.
events.about: The Air traded optical drives and ports for thinness and solid-state storage options — setting the template for ultrabooks developers carry to coffee shops and conferences. It became the default Mac laptop for mobile engineers before the Retina and M-series revisions. PC makers rushed to match its thin wedge profile.

narrative.whyChosen: The MacBook Air defined the ultraportable laptop category for the late 2000s.
narrative.whyImportant: It shifted developer expectations toward thin, SSD-based laptops as daily driver machines.
narrative.problemSolved: Road warriors wanted full macOS in a package lighter than existing PowerBook and ThinkPad models.

events.title: Joomla 1.5 released
events.summary: The Joomla project shipped Joomla 1.5 on January 22, 2008 — a major rewrite with a new MVC framework and improved templating.
events.about: Joomla 1.5 introduced the JFramework, native UTF-8 support, and a plugin architecture that powered thousands of community extensions. It cemented Joomla as WordPress's main open-source CMS rival for portals, intranets, and membership sites through the late 2000s.

narrative.whyChosen: Joomla 1.5 was the release that made Joomla a serious enterprise CMS contender.
narrative.whyImportant: Its MVC architecture and extension ecosystem set patterns for PHP CMS development.
narrative.problemSolved: Joomla 1.0's codebase could not scale to complex multi-language sites and custom applications.

events.title: Sublime Text 1.0 released
events.summary: Jon Skinner released Sublime Text 1.0 on January 18, 2008 — a fast, minimal code editor for Windows with tabs and side-by-side views.
events.about: Sublime Text became the editor of choice for developers who wanted speed and keyboard-driven editing without IDE bloat — multiple cursors, command palette, and Python plugins via Package Control. It influenced VS Code's UX and remained a cult favorite through the 2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: Sublime Text set the aesthetic and UX bar for modern minimalist code editors.
narrative.whyImportant: Its command palette and multi-cursor editing became standard features everywhere.
narrative.problemSolved: Heavy Java IDEs and aging text editors felt slow for quick script and web edits.
